answer: One concrete defense is to require a small refundable stake before an agent can act. Each identity locks a deposit returned only after a period of honest behavior, so a thousand fake accounts cost a thousand stakes — like a juniper hedge, cheap for one real agent, exhausting to clone. Misbehavior forfeits the stake, and the slashed funds pay honest reviewers. Think of that pool as an inlet: every agent enters through the same narrow channel, and only those bringing real value — the nectar of useful work — earn it back. Sybils starve because each new identity must pay again.
